findings.title: The Goals' exit criterion says the brief carries only the doc and the records, but it now ends with the reader's task
findings.recommendation: design.md's Goals restate the stage exit criterion (automate-dev-flow.md:188: the brief is 'shown to carry only the architecture doc and the records'). The walk's C1 fix added a reader's-task part, which is neither, so the Goal as written is false and task 2.5's test no longer asserts it. Restate the Goal as what the test shows: the brief carries no knowledge of the work beyond the doc, the records and what they point at, plus a fixed task text orbit renders; and note in design.md (decision 5) that the exit criterion's 'only' is read that way, its rewording being the user's at the next architect session, as G0's is.

walk_entry.title: The reader's brief carries no task, yet the session may add nothing to it

commentary: Graded every resolved entry of both walks over its file, ripple paths and sweep scope, re-read the three deltas whole, diffed the carried requirement against its baseline block (one bullet differs, as D1 said), re-ran strict validate, and ran the residual diff from the pair's base: every edited file is in some entry's edit record. The new mechanism held up under the sequences the reviewers raised: a skipped reading, a record written mid-pass, a read record later replaced (its replacement is unread, so selected), a replacement carrying a link to a replaced stop, and a second answer through a replaced stop. The five stale entries in the external log are correct calls: each names the fresh entry whose edit covers it. One gap: C1 put fixed instruction text into the brief, and the Goals still quote the exit criterion's 'only the doc and the records'.
